misconceptions.description: Treating specification gaming as a bug in the optimizer rather than a property of under-specified goals
misconceptions.trigger: learner says 'fix the optimizer' in response to specification-gaming examples
misconceptions.feedback: The optimizer is doing its job. The reward function is the lossy hypothesis. Replace the reward function with a better one, or design oversight that catches divergence; do not blame the optimizer.

misconceptions.description: Believing a useful metric will remain useful when it becomes the optimization target
misconceptions.trigger: learner deploys a system that optimizes engagement, expecting engagement to track value
misconceptions.feedback: Goodhart's law: under optimization pressure, the proxy diverges from the underlying property. Plan for divergence; monitor against ground truth signals.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a more capable system is automatically better aligned
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues that scaling solves alignment
misconceptions.feedback: Capability and alignment are independent. Scaling capability without commensurate alignment investment increases the risk of capable misalignment.

misconceptions.description: Claiming a single technique (RLHF, interpretability, governance) solves AI safety
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites one technique as the safety answer
misconceptions.feedback: Each family of intervention addresses some failure modes. The combination is the current best answer and is still being refined. No single technique is sufficient.
